proof_summary: Take the counterexample index $27$: for every base $k\ge2$, $k^{27}-27=(k^9-3)(k^{18}+3k^9+9)$ is a product of two factors greater than $1$, while $k=0,1$ cannot yield a prime of the required form, so no such prime exists. Yet $27$ is not the square of an even integer (every such square is divisible by $4$).
